Welcome to Parsons Down Partnership of Schools
Our Partnership is made up of Parsons Down Infant School and Parsons Down Junior School, and I am delighted to introduce myself as the Interim Headteacher. My name is Miss Alice Mills, and I have the privilege of leading this wonderful community.
At Parsons Down Partnership of Schools, we believe that every child belongs, is valued and has the opportunity to flourish.
Through an inclusive and nurturing community, we support every child's mental and physical wellbeing, enabling them to develop confidence, resilience and a lifelong love of learning.
Our active, ambitious curriculum inspires curiosity and broadens horizons. We provide rich opportunities for children to explore the world around them, experience different cultures and perspectives, and develop an understanding of diversity. By encouraging kindness, respect and tolerance, we prepare our children to become compassionate, responsible citizens who celebrate difference and contribute positively to society.
Together, we foster high aspirations, helping every child to develop the knowledge, skills and character they need to lead healthy, happy and fulfilling lives.
Learn together. Grow together. Succeed together.
What We Aim to Achieve
Our curriculum is designed to ensure that every child develops the knowledge, skills and understanding needed to succeed in school and beyond. Whilst fulfilling the requirements of the National Curriculum, we go beyond statutory expectations by providing rich, meaningful learning experiences that reflect our local community while broadening children's horizons.
· deliver an ambitious, active curriculum that inspires curiosity, creativity and a love of learning;
· provide experiences that deepen children's understanding of the wider world, different cultures and diverse communities;
· nurture confident, resilient learners who are equipped to make healthy choices and develop positive relationships;
· foster respect, empathy and tolerance so that children value difference and contribute positively to society;
· ensure every child, regardless of their starting point, is supported and challenged to achieve their very best.
Through these experiences, we prepare children not only for the next stage of their education but also for happy, healthy and fulfilling lives.
We hope our website provides a useful insight into life at Parsons Down, showcasing our curriculum, strong values, and sense of community that shape our schools. However, nothing compares to experiencing it for yourself. Visits to the school are warmly welcomed, and we would be delighted to show you around. Please contact the school office on 01635 866700 to arrange a visit or to find out more.
Thank you for taking the time to learn more about our Partnership. We look forward to working closely with you as your child continues their learning journey.
​INTERIM HEADTEACHER

Parsons Down Partnership of Schools
Parsons Down Partnership was formed on 4th February 2013 when Parsons Down Infant and Junior Schools officially became a Federation under one Executive Headteacher and one governing body. The schools are officially two schools but work as one community.
To secure the financial future of the Partnership, we have worked closely with the local authority and have reduced our Pupil Admission Number (PAN) from two form (60) to one form from September 2021. Once located in three buildings we have consolidated the three buildings into one building on the site of the Junior School. The remodelled building was officially opened in September 2022 with all pupils being educated in the main building.
The school currently has 225 pupils on roll from EYFS to Year 6 and they are taught in 8 single age year group classes across the Partnership. Our staff are very experienced and many have had a long association with Parsons Down.
The school sits in extensive grounds and is very proud to be an accredited Eco School. In January 2026 we also became a gold standard accredited OPAL (Outdoor Play and Learning) school. We also hold a Gold Games Mark. Opportunities for pupil leadership have been crucial in attaining these accreditations. We have a very active Eco Council, School Council and systems of Year 6 House Captains and monitors.

Meet Our Governors
Harry James
Harry James has extensive experience in school governance. He was a National Leader of Governance Advocate for the south of England overseeing the work of NLGs in that area supporting chairs of governors, chairs of trusts and governing and trust boards across the whole range of their duties.
Harry has chaired boards in a wide range of settings including; a Multi Academy Trust of Special schools, mainstream primary and secondary schools, Alternative Provisions and Pupil Referral Units, and a 6th Form College. He has also chaired a number of Interim Executive Boards.
He has conducted numerous External Reviews of Governance (ERGs) of all types of school and Multi Academy Trusts. He has been an external advisor for Headteacher recruitment and performance management; and has led various panels such as complaints investigations, disciplinary and appeals.
Harry is a founder member of IGoVs (Independent Governor Services) which is a team of ex NLGs who support governing boards across the country. He has been a coach and mentor for the Teach First programme, was a contributor to the Department of Education's Governance Handbook, and co-author of the DfE's SEND Governance Review Guide.
Harry was a trustee of Education Support, a charity that helps all education staff; and is currently chair of West Berkshire Citizens Advice.
Before taking early retirement, he was Director of Communication for The Post Office.
Mary Davies
Mary is an experienced school and Trust leader, having held three Headships and served as a CEO.
She is a current Ofsted Inspector with strong expertise in safeguarding, SEND, curriculum, behaviour and leadership development. She currently supports schools across the South East and Midlands with improvement and governance.
Andy Johnson
Andy is Director of Education for Maiden Erlegh Trust, a family of 11 primary, secondary and special schools across Berkshire and South Oxfordshire. In this role he is responsible for the quality of education provision of around 5000 children and the professional development and support for over 800 staff.
A former secondary RE teacher and Headteacher, Andy has over 20 years of experience in school leadership and school and academy trust development. He holds an MSc in managing school improvement, with a particular research interest in staff professional learning.
Andy has been a part of a number of governing boards and IEBs and is an experienced contracted Ofsted team inspector. He also supports the wider system as an experienced facilitator on the NPQH programme and is a trained leadership coach.
Gus Marriott
Before coming to work for the Local Authority, I worked in a local primary school in a range of roles, from phase lead, to curriculum lead, to headteacher.
In 2024, I came to join West Berkshire Council as our Virtual School Head, with a duty to support the education experiences and outcomes for our children in care and those supported by Children's Services. This role requires me to have a secure and up-to-date knowledge of the education system and pedagogy, inclusive practice in schools, and my work has already improved outcomes for the children in care we support.
I am also currently supporting the Rees Centre (University of Oxford) with their research into relational inclusion in schools, and am one of the lead Virtual School Heads developing an effective self-evaluation tool for Local Authority Virtual Schools, working in collaboration with the National Association for Virtual School Heads (NAVSH) and a regional group of professionals.
Julia Mead
Julia Mead is the Chief Strategy Officer at The Keys Academy Trust (TKAT), a primary specialist Multi Academy Trust in Berkshire. Prior to this role, she served as Chief Finance Officer at TKAT for 8 years from the Trust’s incorporation in 2017 until August 2025. TKAT is a family of thirteen distinctive schools rooted at the heart of the communities they serve and is committed to securing the very best educational outcomes for the pupils in the Trust.
Julia is a Chartered Accountant, having trained with Ernst & Young, where she spent 10 years in the audit department. She brings over 18 years' experience in education finance, in both local authority-maintained schools and academy schools.
She has extensive governance experience, having served on the Interim Executive Board for a sponsor school and a new free school in Wokingham. In addition, she has been a Staff Governor at a maintained school for 8 years.
Julia is an experienced finance professional, with extensive knowledge within the education sector and has a strong track record of supporting school improvement through effective financial leadership.

Reading
How do we teach reading at Parsons Down?
We have developed a ‘reading culture’ at Parsons Down, where children can interact with books, print and spoken language. We promote the enjoyment of a wide range of genres and encourage children’s own interests. Great importance is placed on ‘reading for meaning’ and a variety of methods are used to develop children’s skills in reading through a host of learning experiences.
The teaching of reading begins in the autumn term of Foundation Stage where the children are introduced to letter sounds (not letter names), and over the course of the term, become familiar with all the initial sounds of the letters of the alphabet. These are not taught in alphabetical order, but follow the order prescribed in the RWI Phonics programme.
Once the children are confident of the initial sounds they are taught to segment the letters in words in order to decode (read) and blend letters in order to encode (write). The children usually begin to do this when ready in the Foundation Stage, following the structure of the RWI Phonics programme and are grouped according to their rate of progress.
In Years 1 and 2 the children continue to follow the programme, again working in groups determined by rate of progress. During their English sessions, as well as revising and learning new phonic sounds, the children will apply and develop their phonic and reading skills whilst reading a range of phonic books, both fiction and non-fiction. As well as phonic lessons the children all receive Whole Class Reading Sessions where they are encouraged to develop the ability to read at speed, with fluency and expression, and to read ‘like a story-teller’ and discuss many aspects of the book in order to answer comprehension questions verbally. The content of these books becomes gradually more complex.
​​Once pupils are able to decode, their reading continues and we begin working on the pupils’ comprehension skills. Comprehension skills are taught through a whole school reading programme. This develops children’s comprehension of, and response to, a variety of texts so that they become critical thinkers engaging with texts. Comprehension activities are designed to help children to infer, summarise, question, clarify, predict and argue a point of view. The children also make connections between texts and their own experiences. We use higher order questioning to ensure pupils reach age related expectations and are well challenged.
Throughout the school, from Foundation Stage to Year 6, children are provided with reading books from the Read Write Inc (Bookbag Books matched to phonics assessment) and reading for pleasure books (closely matched to their ability) Oxford Reading Tree and Treetops schemes, to share with an adult at home. We expect that children read at home with an adult at least four times per week, to extend the ‘reading culture’ beyond school itself. Children are heard read in school by an adult regularly and are guided in their book choices.
The children also have access to the library and visit it every week to borrow a book of their choosing.

Mathematics
We believe that mathematics is important in everyday life and to be successful mathematicians, we provide our children the opportunity to build on prior knowledge, develop their resilience when presented with challenges whilst shaping positive attitudes towards the subject.
Our aim is to develop all pupils’ mathematical thinking, fluency and reasoning skills through high quality, daily lessons by delivering the mastery approach. Through this, we develop children’s ability to problem solve, reason as well as think and work systematically. Our curriculum caters for the needs of all individuals as well as providing challenge which sets our pupils up to be confident, flexible mathematicians. The CPA approach (concrete, pictorial, abstract) allows children to have hands-on learning through manipulatives that encourages mathematical thinking, development of language and steadily builds deeper understanding.
By using the mastery approach, we have a focus on developing fluency, reasoning and problem solving skills. We break our lessons down into small steps which secures knowledge of concepts. Questioning is used to deepen understanding and develop mathematical connections and fluency. Stem sentences, using mathematical language, allows children to verbalise and explain their thinking.
